sources.role: Identifies the native application and its 2007 method.

Published author-hosted paper: triangular administration hazards, actual-history likelihood, approximate lognormal prior elicitation, posterior safety and nearest-target allocation; page 116 defines grade-2 persistence or attributed dose-reduction qualification with event time at onset.
Original2.2.0 installer, guide, managed saved-file schema and bounded native references; assets excluded from redistribution.

implementation_choices: Discrete zero-based dose indices and nested candidate schedules; actual patient histories may have variable doses and irregular administration times.
Independent Gaussian priors on log hazard-area increments, log peak time and log tail duration. Zero standard deviations explicitly fix coordinates in reduced models.
Paper moment elicitation is approximate: it uses a transformed mean toxicity and assumes completed per-administration hazard when relating shortest-schedule risk to total area.
Posterior fitting uses bounded serial elliptical slice sampling rather than reproducing the native coordinate Metropolis sampler or its random-number stream.
Each regimen risk is evaluated directly. Ordered total areas alone do not ensure finite-horizon risk ordering when peak times and tail durations differ.
Safety uses a strict toxicity-tail event and a strict upper probability cutoff. Exact selection ties use lowest dose then shortest schedule.

No-skip policies are explicit Python conventions for ambiguous histories: coordinate_max uses separate largest tried coordinates; observed_pair requires a candidate to be at most one level above both coordinates of a tried pair.

The first assignment defaults to the lowest pair and bypasses posterior exclusion while retaining the computed safety mask. An alternative starting pair is a Python extension. Final selection requires prior treatment and removes no-skip restrictions; the caller ensures completed follow-up.

Delayed toxicity conduct takes explicit episode adjudication times and qualification decisions. Only available adjudications enter an as-of fit; qualifying events are backdated to onset, actual delivered doses remain separately visible, and unresolved earlier onsets prevent final readiness.

The grade-2 helper applies the paper's persistence-or-attributed-dose-reduction rule using caller-supplied observed resolution/reduction times. Exact-deadline ascertainment is an explicit Python convention: resolution at or before 14 days is nonqualifying absent an attributed reduction; still unresolved at the deadline qualifies. Snapshots must be recomputed at each analysis. The paper does not specify a stochastic low-grade episode process or an automatic native adjudication clock.

Current desktop guide workflows are integrated in dose_schedule_desktop_* modules with separate safe and desktop_legacy controllers, actual histories, scenario simulation, captured-input reports and posterior draw export.

Original native prior/controller/observation/lognormal/schedule/final-clock probes and original managed serializer fixture are portable and hash-pinned. See research/dose-schedule-desktop-recovery-2026-10-12.md.

Native first assignment, cutoff equality, propagated exclusions, final no-skip and fixed14-day qualification are explicit legacy rules. Safe final conduct waits for observed horizon/adjudication and rejects incomplete censoring.
limitations: Full desktop workflow acceptance is in progress. Python posterior integration and supplied CDF-oriented random tapes do not claim native integration/RNG stream identity. Current guide nu calibration and generated low-grade law are recovered; the separate2013 automatic within-patient policy is not substituted. Source compatibility, numerical correctness and clinical validity are distinct.
